evaluations.verdict: The sturdiest pure-ring colour icon: one bold die-cut sticker on amber that stays a crisp rainbow C at 16px, handles dark mode cleanly, and brings the best functional idea in the round (a live notch that widens as the timer runs). But the notch, the concept's whole signature, is a 1px dent at tray size. The template collapses into a heavy donut that outweighs Wi-Fi and battery and reads as 'record' or 'O' rather than 'timer'.
evaluations.riff: Redraw the template at SF Symbols regular weight (ring about 12% of diameter). Deepen the spent notch into a clear wedge bridged by a 1.5pt track so the silhouette stays closed (no spinner read) but the notch survives at 16px and can animate as the live timer. Or plug the gap with starcap's star as the finish-line crown.

evaluations.verdict: The truest story in the set: the app's own hamster (checked against the reference, it's faithful) really does ride the leading cap, and at Dock size it reads as 'the rainbow timer with the runner'. It falls apart where the client needs it most. At 32/16 the hamster is a brown speck on a big empty dish, and the template is a thin/thick ring with a lump at the bottom that reads as a fishbowl or moon phase, not a hamster.
evaluations.riff: Make the hamster about three times larger and stand it on top of the ring at 12 o'clock, so its head and ears break the outer silhouette. The glyph then becomes a ring with a critter crown: a stopwatch at 18px, a hamster at 36px.

evaluations.verdict: The most complete system this round: the star gives the rainbow ring a focal point and a classroom meaning, the colour icon stays balanced down to 16px, and the template is the only one drawn at a weight that sits happily beside SF Symbols. At 18pt it reads as a stopwatch with its crown, exactly the right meaning for a tray item. Two weaknesses: the spent gap mostly hides under the star, so it reads as a full timer rather than a countdown, and the star is a generic gold star, not the app's orange sticker.
evaluations.riff: Swap in the app's actual orange star sticker (its gradient, thick white border, a tilt in 5° steps) and widen the spent gap to the left of the star (10 to 12 o'clock) so it still counts down. Enlarge the glyph's star by about 30% so its points survive at 18px @2x instead of becoming a nub.

evaluations.verdict: A friendly, toy-like colour icon that holds up at 16px, but the blocks look nothing like the app's smooth ring. The template is a dashed circle, which every Mac and GNOME user reads as a loading or sync spinner, the one thing a status item must not look like. It is also the rejected dot grid bent into a circle, and the hollow 'spent' socket turns to grey mush at 1x.
evaluations.riff: Use a solid ring for the resting mark and keep the segments only for the live running state (blocks drop out as time passes), so the menu-bar item never sits idle looking like a spinner.

evaluations.verdict: The most tasteful icon and the closest match to the sage, terracotta and rose UI, but it's the direction the client already rejected: nothing on it is what teachers see. The muted ring on deep sage loses contrast at 32/16, with visible conic-gradient streaks, and would flatten in tinted mode, where rose and sage have similar luminance. It reads as a meditation or budgeting app.
evaluations.riff: Don't ship it as a separate concept. Fold the palette into master as an alternate Dock icon (a settings toggle that sets NSApp.applicationIconImage) or as the dark variant, and raise the value contrast between rose and sage so it survives tinted mode and 16px.

evaluations.verdict: The most ownable, lovable Dock icon here: the hamster matches the app's own (orange oval body, tan head, round orange ears, dot eyes, curly tail), it pops in dark mode, and no other app has it. But the hamster now dominates the ring, so it reads 'pet app' before 'timer'. The template (a critter with eye holes, feet and tail inside a 250° open arc) clogs at 1x and flirts with a refresh arrow.
evaluations.riff: Simplify the template hamster to a solid silhouette (head, two ears and body; no eye holes, feet or tail curl). Close the arc into a full thin ring with a 1 to 1.5pt spent track, so it reads as 'creature in a timer' at 16px instead of a rotate/refresh icon.

evaluations.verdict: A faithful portrait of the name picker and the only idea that isn't a ring. But it copies a UI panel into a squircle, which the HIG warns against; the white chip with a black bar reads as a minus button or text field; and the rainbow timer the client asked for is gone. The boxed three-pill template is the heaviest glyph in the set and looks like a drawer, a server, or Control Center's toggles in the macOS menu bar.
evaluations.riff: Let the chosen chip break out of the reel: oversized, tilted and die-cut, overlapping the window frame, with confetti. The silhouette then becomes the 'picked!' moment instead of a UI card, and the glyph gets an ownable shape (a pill bursting through a frame) instead of a boxed list.

evaluations.verdict: It has the only ring that truly matches the in-app timer (timer.tsx's real conic gradient). But bolting a glossy traffic light onto the side makes two marks instead of the one the client asked for, pushes the composition off-centre and cools the palette. The template is an open C (reads as a spinner) plus a 3px pill whose lights collapse into a grey bar at 16 to 18px.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light and give the true conic gradient, with the thinner in-app ring proportion, to the master/diecut sticker. If a second widget must appear, show it as colour (traffic-light green on the leading cap), not as a second object.

evaluations.verdict: Polished and the safest at 32/16, but it's the most generic ring in the set: a flat-banded rainbow donut that reads as a colour picker. The claimed 15° sticker tilt is invisible because a circle has no orientation. The template is a nearly solid disc with an irregular knockout, the heaviest ring glyph, and it reads as an eye or an appearance toggle next to the clock.
evaluations.riff: Give the die-cut a non-circular edge so it reads as a sticker: peel it up where time has been spent (a lifted, shadowed flap at the upper left). That also gives the glyph a distinctive flat-chord silhouette. Otherwise, merge it into master.

general: Eight of nine concepts are rings and seven share the same amber squircle; master, brandring and diecut are essentially one drawing. The ring is the right place to converge, since it's the most recognisable and scalable idea, but the thick hard-banded donut drifts toward colour-picker and Google territory and away from the app's thinner conic-gradient ring. The recurring failure is the menu-bar glyph: most are too heavy (master, brandring, diecut, reel) or too detailed (hamcap, mascot, ringplus), open arcs and dashed rings read as refresh or loading spinners, and only starcap pairs SF Symbols weight with a clear 'timer' meaning. Four things are missing from every sheet: the macOS 26 tinted and clear appearances (where the rainbow drops out and the silhouette has to carry identity), a plate-less die-cut version for Windows 11 and GNOME, a demo of master's live-progress glyph, and any nod to the name picker in the timer concepts. Next round should settle on one ring, add one ownable anchor at 12 o'clock (the app's real orange star versus the faithful hamster breaking the outline), draw the glyph at SF Symbols regular weight, and prototype the live countdown state; all nine followed the no-numerals and faithful-hamster rules, so no concept was penalised.

evaluations.verdict: This is the most system-ready mark in the set. The thick 250° band gives the best colour mass at 16/32 and in the favicon, and the die-cut notch keeps the white 16px tray glyph a single closed, heavy shape that no Wi-Fi, volume or spinner symbol shares; the widening-notch live state can be driven by Shell_NotifyIcon, AppIndicator and NSStatusItem alike. Weak spots: at 16px the notch is only a ~2px step, so the glyph drifts toward 'lumpy donut'; it is much heavier than Windows 11's 1px line tray icons; and the flat six-band palette reads a bit like Google next to a Google Classroom tab.
evaluations.riff: Hand-tune the tray glyph at 16, 20 and 24px: cut the notch as a clean step at least 3px deep and slim the band to ~3px, so it reads as a cut ring rather than a lump and sits closer to Fluent/GNOME stroke weight. Then ship the widening notch as the tray's running-timer state.

evaluations.verdict: At 128–256 it is the most literal picture of the running timer, and the hamster really is the app's own (so the rule is met). But everything it is about disappears below 48px: at 32/16 the rider is a brown smudge, and the thin ring leaves the favicon with little colour. The tray glyph is a 1–2px ring with a lump at the bottom, too light for GNOME symbolic, and it reads as something sitting in a bowl rather than a rider.
evaluations.riff: Merge with master using different art per size: master's thick notched ring and glyph at 16–32 and in the tray, with the hamster riding the leading cap only in the 48–256 .ico/.icns frames, where it can actually be seen.

evaluations.verdict: Warm and very classroom: a closed ring plus the gold-star sticker. It survives as a 16px favicon (ring plus yellow dot), and the star stays inside the maskable safe zone (it reaches 0.38 of the icon width; the limit is 0.40). In monochrome the star shrinks to a 2px bump at 12 o'clock, so the tray glyph is crisp and correctly weighted beside Windows/GNOME status icons but reads as a generic stopwatch crown (like Fluent's 'Timer' or SF Symbols' 'stopwatch'): easy to read, but not ownable.
evaluations.riff: Merge with master: move the star off 12 o'clock into master's spent-time notch (~10 o'clock). The colour icon keeps its gold star, and the glyph trades the stopwatch crown for master's ownable notched outline.

evaluations.verdict: A ring of six blobs is the universal busy/loading spinner. White on a dark taskbar at 16px it tells teachers the app is stuck, it is a close cousin of the dot grid the client wants gone, and the hollow 'spent' block dissolves into 1px mush. The colour icon keeps its dots of colour at 16px, but it reads as a colour wheel or a Trivial Pursuit pie, not the smooth timer ring teachers see.
evaluations.riff: Retire it. If the toy-block feel matters, fold it into master as faint seams on a continuous band, so the glyph stays one closed shape.

evaluations.verdict: Master's structure and identical glyph in the true brand colours: the best palette fit, and a sage plate that would stand out in a dock full of blue icons. But it is not what teachers see, and at 16px the sage-teal leading cap melts into the sage plate, so the ring becomes a muddy rose-brown donut chart that looks like a finance or wellness app. The deep plate also sinks on dark Windows taskbars and the GNOME dash.
evaluations.riff: Demote it to master's calm alternate (a dark-mode or in-app accent version). If it must lead, make the plate two steps lighter and push the leading cap to a pale sage-cream, so it separates from the plate at 16px and on dark taskbars.

evaluations.verdict: The strongest character icon here: at 48–256 the app's own hamster sitting in the rainbow ring is instantly the timer (rule met), and it would be memorable in a GNOME/KDE app grid. Below 32px it turns to mush, and the tray glyph is the wrong shape for a tray: an open, round-capped arc around a hamster blob reads as a refresh/history arrow (think Time Machine), and the 1px eye cut-outs fill in at 16px.
evaluations.riff: Keep the centred hamster for the 48–256 frames and the dock/app grid, but give the 16–32 sizes and the tray glyph to master's closed notched ring. The open arc has to go either way.

evaluations.verdict: The only concept that breaks away from the ring: the lilac-pink-butter slot card is clearly the name picker at 64+, the card stays just inside the 80% maskable circle (measured 0.398 of width, limit 0.40), and its glyph is the crispest in the set, snapped to the pixel grid at Windows 11 line weight. But at 16px the colour icon is a pink card with a minus sign, and the glyph's 1px outlined side pills read as a server, drawer or robot face: too thin for GNOME symbolic, and nothing says 'picker'.
evaluations.riff: Add the slot machine's pointer notches either side of the chosen chip and make the top and bottom pills solid 2px bars, so the 16px glyph reads as a picker rather than a server or filing cabinet.

evaluations.verdict: It has the most faithful ring (the real conic gradient from timer.tsx) plus a real widget, but the two-part layout halves both at 32/16, and the traffic light shrinks to a dark sliver. The tray glyph is the weakest in the set: an open C-shaped spinner beside a 3px dotted column that reads as 'O8' or a battery, right next to 'ENG 9:41'.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light and give ringplus's genuine timer.tsx conic gradient to master's notched ring.

evaluations.verdict: Clean, heavy and closed: the solid die-cut disc makes a well-weighted GNOME-symbolic glyph, and the colour icon is the most literal timer widget (cream face, white rim, rainbow arc on amber). But it is also the most generic, a Google-coloured progress ring on a plate whose 15° tilt can't be seen on a circle, and at 16px the glyph reads as a donut or an eyeball rather than a timer.
evaluations.riff: On Windows and Linux, drop the plate and ship the round die-cut sticker itself (with its soft shadow) as an object-style icon, which both Fluent and GNOME prefer. Keep the amber plate only for macOS and the PWA maskable icon. That is the one thing it can do better than master.

general: Seven of the nine are the same rainbow ring on the same amber plate, so the colour side has converged; what really separates them is the 16px tray. There, only closed, single-shape outlines survive (master/brandring, starcap, diecut), and every added element (hamster, traffic light, blocks, side pills) collapses into a lump, a spinner or an 'O8'; no concept breaks the no-numerals or hamster rules. The flat red-orange-yellow-green-blue-purple bands appear in five concepts and look Google-ish at favicon size in a tab row full of Google Classroom and Drive; the app's own conic gradient, used only by ringplus, is a more ownable colour source. Missing entirely: different art per size (.ico and .icns frames can hold a different drawing at 16–32 than at 48–256, which is how to keep the hamster or star without wrecking small sizes), glyph weights per platform (1px line on Windows 11, 2px symbolic on GNOME, macOS template), plate-less object versions for Windows 11 and GNOME, and tray mock-ups beside real Wi-Fi/volume/battery icons and in Windows high-contrast mode. The next round should stop inventing new shapes: lock master's notched ring, hand-tune its glyph at 16/20/24px with a deeper notch, test the real conic gradient, use the hamster or star only as a large-size accent, and make the widening notch the tray's live running-timer state.

evaluations.verdict: The hardiest mark in the set: the flat six-band ring, stepped die-cut notch and bold notched-O glyph hold at every size, and it's the right base for the identity. On its own, though, it's the safe choice. With an empty face and no runner it's 'a rainbow donut', which the wider world reads as a colour wheel or progress ring and a school reads as 'a timer app', so only the amber plate and the notch are really ownable.
evaluations.riff: Keep this ring, notch and glyph as the base and add ONE owned co-hero at real scale: the round-2 Gold Star Timer's big tilted die-cut star slapped over the lower-right of the ring. Separately, actually build the promised live notch, and test a lockup where the ring replaces the first 'o' in 'Classroom'.

evaluations.verdict: The most faithful copy of the live widget, with the app's hamster exactly as drawn, but the hamster is under a third of the plate's width and tucked low, so from 64 px down the brand's best asset is a brown smudge on a rainbow ring. The glyph (a circle with a blob at the bottom) reads as an avatar badge or fishbowl, and a hamster running inside a wheel hands critics the 'hamster wheel' idiom for teacher busywork.
evaluations.riff: Fold it into mascot: use the rider pose as the running-timer loading animation and splash moment, not the icon. If it stays an icon, enlarge the hamster until it breaks over the rim and becomes the silhouette.

evaluations.verdict: This grew out of the client's favourite, the Gold Star Timer, and lost what made that one work. The star shrank from a tilted co-hero slapped across the face to a topper at 12 o'clock, so the icon reads as a rainbow wreath or bauble (the star is a yellow dot at 16 px), and the ring-with-a-bump glyph reads as a power button, stopwatch or cartoon bomb.
evaluations.riff: Go back to the round-2 size and gesture: a star about half the ring's width, tilted 10–15°, overlapping ring and rim at 4–5 o'clock with a thick white die-cut border, on master's notched flat-band ring. In the glyph, cut the star in at lower-right with a wide gap, never perched at 12.

evaluations.verdict: Friendly and toy-like, but it stops looking like the app, whose timer is one continuous ring. The blocks read as a colour palette, pill organiser or game spinner, a circle of multicolour rounded pills is Slack and Google Photos territory, and the dashed-circle glyph is the universal loading spinner, the worst possible message from a tray icon.
evaluations.riff: Drop it as the icon. Keep the break-into-blocks idea only as a 'time's up' animation on master's continuous ring.

evaluations.verdict: The only concept in the brand's own UI palette and the most grown-up for docs and decks, but it gives up the recognition the client asked for: teachers see a bright rainbow on amber, not a dusty gradient on forest green. The rose-to-sage sweep reads as a red-to-green status gauge, the ring melts into the plate at 16 px, and a green 'Classroom…' favicon next to Google Classroom's green tab invites a 'Google add-on' misreading.
evaluations.riff: Make it the calm secondary version (docs, print, the one-colour logo, the macOS tinted appearance) and keep amber plus rainbow as the main icon, so the dock matches the board.

evaluations.verdict: The strongest brand platform this round. It turns the no-numeral rule into the idea (the hamster lives where the number was), it's the only mark with a face, and it's the app's own hamster, so users know it on sight. A character like this extends into loading, empty and 'Time's up!' states, docs and merch, the way ClassDojo's and Duolingo's do, and none of the big names here (Google Classroom, Canva, Notion, Slack, Microsoft 365) leads with one. The weak link is the glyph, a critter blob with pin-hole eyes inside an open arc that reads as critter-plus-refresh at 16–18 px, and it risks looking too primary-school for secondary teachers.
evaluations.riff: Close the glyph's arc into master's notched ring so it can't read as a refresh arrow, and redraw the glyph hamster as a bold side profile (ears, tail, feet, no pin-hole eyes). In the colour icon, let a foot and the tail overlap the ring so the hamster sits in the timer rather than inside a badge.

evaluations.verdict: A welcome break from the sea of rings, and the name picker is the app's second-strongest memory, but it's hard to own. The lilac-pink-butter gradient in a rounded frame sits in Instagram's gradient territory, the chosen chip's black dash reads as a minus sign or toggle, the glyph is a generic framed stack (server, drawer, list), and it drops the rainbow timer the client named first.
evaluations.riff: Use it as the randomiser's feature icon and a marketing moment. If the picker has to be in the main mark, lay one bright name chip across master's ring like a label instead of drawing a separate card.

evaluations.verdict: Two icons glued together, not one idea. The smooth rainbow gradient pulls the ring towards colour-picker and 'AI glow' icons (Apple Intelligence, Copilot), the glossy traffic light is the most generic widget the app has, and the glyph spells 'Ɔ8' (refresh plus battery), with the light shrinking to a black sliver at 16 px.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light and the smooth gradient. If a second widget earns a place, fuse something only this app has (a die-cut sticker or the name chip) into the ring instead of parking it alongside.

evaluations.verdict: The most literal portrait of the in-app timer and the cleanest favicon in the set, but the least ownable. A closed white disc with a flat-band rainbow ring is the generic progress ring (at 16 px it sits in the same family as Chrome's multicolour ring), and the 15° sticker tilt is invisible because a rotated circle is still a circle, so the sticker idea never comes across.
evaluations.riff: Give the die-cut a non-round outline so the tilt and the 'sticker' read, for example the white border swelling around a big attached gold star (merging with the Gold Star Timer), or fold it into master.

evaluations.verdict: (Round 2 #5, Gold Star Timer, the client's pick.) The only concept across two rounds with a gesture: a teacher has just slapped the app's own die-cut star onto the timer. 'Gold star' is the one praise idiom every teacher shares, so this is the easiest mark to name and to hand out as merch (print it as a real sticker), and it presents the product as time plus praise, not just a timer. As drawn, though, the grey C-plus-star glyph reads as a crescent and star at 18 px, a religious and national symbol that appears on both Singapore's and Malaysia's flags. The grey also reads as a disabled menu item, and at 16 px the favicon is just an orange star beside the browser's own bookmark star.
evaluations.riff: Take it to final on master's notched flat-band ring, with at least 270° of ring showing and the star as co-hero at lower-right. The glyph becomes a solid ring with the star separated by a wide gap, so it can only read as 'star sticker on a timer', never moon-and-star or favourites.

evaluations.verdict: (Round 2 #6, Mini Board, the client's pick.) The richest story and the highest recognition, since it literally is the projected board. As drawn, though, it breaks the no-numeral rule (the 6), four elements compete so there's no single shape to own, it turns to mush at 32 and 16 px, and the grey card + star + C glyph reads as a weather or sync icon. A scene is an illustration, not a mark.
evaluations.riff: Make it the large-size layer of an identity that changes with size: the full board with an empty face for the 512–1024 px icon, the About screen, the website hero and the DMG background, stepping down to ring + star at 32/16 px and sharing the Gold Star Timer's one-colour glyph.

general: Round 3 converged on one answer: six of the nine concepts are the same flat rainbow donut on amber with an empty cream face. They are interchangeable on a dock and generic in the wider world (colour wheel, progress ring, the multicolour loops Google and Microsoft already own, and the visual-countdown look Time Timer made famous in classrooms). What's ownable is the amber/caramel plate (no one owns that colour next to Google Classroom's green, Canva's teal-purple, Slack's aubergine and Notion's black), plus one thing a teacher can name, and only two concepts supply that: mascot's hamster and the client's round-2 Gold Star Timer (starcap shrank that star into a topper and lost the gesture). Next round should use master's notched flat-band ring and solid glyph as the base and put ONE co-hero on it at real size (the big slapped-on gold star, or the hamster), with a one-colour glyph that can't read as a crescent and star, a refresh arrow or an avatar. Then scale the identity by size so the client's two favourites become one system instead of rivals: Mini Board's full scene (face empty) for 512–1024 px, the About screen, the website hero and the DMG background, stepping down to ring + star at 32/16 px and a shared glyph. At the user's request I also scored the round-2 Gold Star Timer and Mini Board under their round-2 slugs 'sticker' and 'board', so 'sticker' in my top 3 is the round-2 Gold Star Timer.
